clue.text: Warm outer covering enfolding Old Bill in bed

indicators.note: the covering wraps around the next piece, so one is set inside the other

parts.note: an animal's fur is its warm outer coat
a bill is a printed notice or poster

explanation.surface: A police officer, the Old Bill, snug under a warm cover in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' looks like British slang for the police, but it splits in two: old and bill; 'enfolding' wraps the warm covering round the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed with a post at each corner, often supporting a canopy, is named after those posts.

clue.text: Decline to produce fashion note

parts.note: a fad is a passing fashion or craze
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Someone resisting the urge to write a note about fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to grow weaker or dimmer, to wither gradually.

clue.text: Showed sadness after good times raised, in a style

indicators.note: the crying comes after the good times, so that piece is placed second

parts.note: ups, as in ups and downs, are good times
someone who wept showed sadness

explanation.surface: Someone who cried once the happy days had been brought up in a stylish way.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair brushed upward and pinned is said to be dressed in an upward-swept style.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory tale a hard-up brother, say, produced

parts.note: poor work is unsatisfactory work
a relation is an account or narrative, a telling of a tale

explanation.surface: A struggling sibling comes up with a feeble story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' here is the old sense of a story told; the definition is the family sense, so the same word serves both readings.
explanation.definitionFit: A penniless family member, such as a brother, is the impoverished kin of the family.

clue.text: Placed when appeal to University is accepted in full

indicators.note: the appeal and the university are taken inside the word for full

parts.note: sated means full, having eaten enough
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A student is placed once their appeal to the university is fully accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' here is the old slang 'it' for sex appeal; 'is accepted in' puts the appeal and the university inside the word for full.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated is located or positioned in a particular spot.

clue.text: Energy and drive one way to detect this self-seeker?

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
go means energy or drive, as in 'full of go'
I is the Roman numeral for one
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A detective's method for spotting a selfish person by their energy and drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to detect this' is padding for the surface: the pieces E, GO, I and ST simply join up in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An egoist puts personal interest first, a selfish person who looks after number one.

clue.text: Political group of leaders in Brussels launching original community

indicators.note: the leaders of the following words are their opening letters, which are taken

explanation.surface: Brussels launches the original European Community, a political grouping.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of nations or parties acting together.

clue.text: Family business on decline

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other, so the business comes first

parts.note: a line is a line of business, a trade
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: A family firm that is going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineage is a line of descent, a family's ancestry.

clue.text: Many abandoned staff in this difficult position

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
left means abandoned
a staff is a walking stick

explanation.surface: Many workers walked out, leaving the firm in a bind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is a walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a forked stick means being trapped in a dilemma with no way to move.

clue.text: Crookedness and underworld wrong-doing one's taking on

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for it
a tort is a civil wrong in law
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gangland crime in which someone is cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the classical underworld; 'one's taking on' gives I then ON, with ''s taking' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A distortion is a twisting out of true shape, a bending away from straight.

clue.text: Joint king born in France

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
née is French for born, used before a maiden name

explanation.surface: A royal birth that brings two houses together in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint between thigh and lower leg.

clue.text: Disaffection between dreadful sergeant and soldiers? Precisely!

indicators.note: a dreadful version of the word is a badly mangled one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: men are ordinary soldiers, as opposed to officers
to a T means precisely, so T stands for it

explanation.surface: Bad feeling between a nasty sergeant and the troops, exactly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' signals the anagram of the eight letters of the soldier's rank; 'between' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement is the cooling or breaking of a relationship, people drifting apart.

clue.text: River sport

definitions.meaning: a river in north-east England flowing through Durham

explanation.definitionFit: The Wear is an English river, and to sport clothing is to have it on.

clue.text: One way to board a vessel with worker giving support

indicators.note: the one and the way follow on after the ship, as passengers step aboard after it arrives

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a vessel
I is the Roman numeral for one
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone climbs aboard a ship, with a deckhand helping them up.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant role is a helping, auxiliary one, lending aid to another.

clue.text: Stands for displays soldiers put on

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldiers are put on top of the other piece

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
presents means shows or displays

explanation.surface: Soldiers stage a show for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to symbolise it or act on its behalf.

clue.text: Former spouse gave a parting ring and cracked up

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
a bell tolled gives a slow ring for a departed person

explanation.surface: A former partner handed back the wedding ring and went to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked up' looks like breaking down, but it means praised, as in 'not all it is cracked up to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack something up is to praise it highly, to laud it.

clue.text: Keen artist backed to make an impression

indicators.note: backed means the word for artist is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a dent is an impression pressed into a surface

explanation.surface: An eager painter, with backing, sets out to make a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionately eager, burning with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Right place in the field to follow heartless mercenary — such as this ruffian

indicators.note: the right and the field place come after the mercenary's remains
a heartless word has lost its middle, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: mid-on is a cricket fielding position

explanation.surface: A hired thug takes up a fielding position, the sort of brute you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: MID-ON is a cricket fielding position near the bowler on the leg side; 'heartless' leaves MY from mercenary.
explanation.definitionFit: A myrmidon is a hired henchman who carries out orders without scruple.

clue.text: Tell the story of City during ceremony

indicators.note: the city sits within the time of the ceremony, so it goes inside

parts.note: a rite is a solemn ceremony
EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone recounts what happened in the City during a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London is the capital's financial district, known by its postcode; 'during' places it inside the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to narrate or give an account of events.

clue.text: Match points are given after brief competition

indicators.note: the word are follows the shortened competition

parts.note: comp is a short form of competition

explanation.surface: In a contest, a short game decides who wins the match points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match points' looks like tennis, but it is the definition: to match points is to set them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To set two sets of points against each other is to weigh their likenesses and differences.

clue.text: Fashionable, we hear, to have short ad — get agent to put one out

indicators.note: we hear means the word for fashionable is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: hip means fashionable

indicators.note: short means a word loses its final letter

parts.note: a notice is a small advertisement

explanation.surface: A trendy advertiser hires someone to knock a person out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns HIP into HYP; 'short' drops the last E from NOTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypnotic is a drug that induces sleep, a soporific that sends someone off.

clue.text: Altered arrangement that can drive machinery

indicators.note: an arrangement of a word puts its letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A rearranged setup that can power machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' signals an anagram of ALTERED; the definition is a thing that can drive machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot pedal that works a lathe or sewing machine.

clue.text: Fury arising from taunt in six-nil hiding

indicators.note: the score of six-nil covers up the taunt, so it is placed inside

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six
O, the zero, stands for nil
to rag is to tease or taunt

explanation.surface: Anger rises from the jeering during a six-nil thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' looks like a heavy defeat in sport but signals that the score wraps round the taunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, violent woman, a shrew or harridan.

clue.text: Academic meeting was a drinking party

definitions.meaning: a conference of scholars discussing a subject
in ancient Greece the word meant a convivial gathering after dinner

explanation.definitionFit: The word now means a scholarly conference but in ancient Greece meant a drinking party.

clue.text: First Lady with new flat

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: The President's wife and a new apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like a president's wife but is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means level and smooth, with no bumps.

clue.text: Hero no longer active, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for inactive is taken by its sound

parts.note: idle means inactive

explanation.surface: A retired champion, it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone admired and adored, a hero-figure.

clue.text: Ungenerous approach

explanation.definitionFit: Near can mean stingy, and to near a place is to come close to it.

clue.text: Free of restraint, unlocked?

definitions.meaning: to go at something in this way is to go all out, without caution
a whimsical reading: without locks of hair

explanation.definitionFit: Going at something like a hairless head means charging recklessly, and a hairless head has no locks.

clue.text: Staunch supporter

definitions.meaning: to ... a flow, such as blood, is to staunch it
a ... supports a flower or leaf

explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding is to stop it, and a plant's stalk holds up its flower.

clue.text: Shabby and on one's uppers — or a bit behind?

definitions.meaning: worn out and impoverished, with worn shoes
a whimsical reading: positioned slightly back, at the foot's rear

explanation.definitionFit: Shoes with worn-down heels mark someone poor and seedy, and the heel is the back of the foot.
